# APS Dashboard — Generic Feature Development Master Prompt (Optimized)

## 1. Purpose

You are working on the **APS Dashboard**, a Google Apps Script Web App used by **Avvaiyar Padasalai**.

Use this prompt for every feature, bug fix, performance improvement, UI change, automation, or maintenance task.

**Primary rule:**
> Read the current code and configuration first → understand the existing flow → reuse existing code → make the smallest safe change → optimize → validate → compare with production → document → report.

Do not assume that a historical note in this prompt is more current than the actual working code.

---

- Read and analyze it; never modify, delete, rename, or overwrite anything inside it.
- Treat it as the production comparison baseline.
- Reuse existing functions, utilities, constants, APIs, UI components, security checks, and patterns whenever safe.
- Preserve existing behavior unless the requested change explicitly requires it.
- Compare the working implementation against this snapshot before completion.

Working project:

`C:\Users\AmChaTS\PycharmProjects\APS-Classroom-Dashboard\`

Primary files:

---

## 4. Existing-Code-First Rule

Before coding:

1. Read the relevant working code and the corresponding production code.
2. Find existing functions that already solve part or all of the problem.
3. Reuse existing:
   - authentication and authorization
   - role resolution
   - Google Sheet helpers
   - Classroom helpers
   - Zoho helpers
   - caching
   - email infrastructure
   - logging/audit
   - date/time utilities
   - UI components
   - modal/tooltip/help systems
   - dropdown/filter behavior
   - validation utilities
   - trigger/configuration helpers
4. Check for existing tests and architecture documentation.
5. Add a new function only when existing functionality cannot safely satisfy the requirement.

Never create duplicate business logic, duplicate APIs, duplicate Sheet reads, duplicate triggers, or duplicate UI components.

---

## 5. Production Safety

**Do not break existing functionality.**

Do not unnecessarily change:
- function names
- API behavior
- Sheet names/headers/column meanings
- role permissions
- URLs
- Classroom behavior
- Zoho behavior
- user workflows
- existing UI behavior
- trigger behavior
- audit/history behavior

Use surgical changes.

Never modify `CURRENT_PROD_CODE`.

---

# 6. Dashboard Performance & Google Sheet Read Optimization — Mandatory for Every Change

Performance is a requirement for **every future feature and bug fix**, not a separate optional task.

**Never trade data accuracy, security, data integrity, or existing functionality for performance.** Do not add new APIs, libraries, frameworks, or external services just for performance. Make **small, surgical, measurable changes**; do not rewrite working code.

### 6.1 Before and after — measure

Before changing code, and again after, identify where practical:
- execution time of the affected server functions
- major Google Sheet reads/writes (which sheet/range, how many times per request)
- `google.script.run` server calls per screen/action
- Classroom / Zoho / other API calls
- payload size returned to the browser
- cache usage (hits, misses, invalidation)
- expensive or repeated processing (loops, scans, sorts, JSON parse/stringify)

Report the difference in the final report (§25, item 7). If measurement is not possible, say so.

### 6.2 Google Sheet reads

Pattern:

`one bulk read → validate/normalize → build indexed lookup maps → process in memory → reuse the result`

- Read each sheet/range **at most once per request**. Pass the values (or the built map) to the functions that need them; do not read the same sheet/range again within the same request.
- Do not call `SpreadsheetApp.open*`, `getSheetByName()`, `getDataRange()`, `getRange()`, `getValues()`, or `getValue()` inside loops or inside helper functions that are called repeatedly when the same data can be read once and reused (pass it in, or memoize it for the current execution).
- Read only the needed range when it is known; avoid `getDataRange()` when a known range is sufficient.
- Use indexed lookup maps (by ID, email, APSID, course ID, etc.) for frequently searched datasets instead of repeatedly filtering/scanning large arrays.
- Never read a Sheet again when the current request already has the data.
- Reuse existing Sheet helpers and the data access steps in §7.

### 6.3 Caching

- Use CacheService for appropriate **non-critical, reusable** data (rules in §14).
- Invalidate or version the cache after **every write** that changes the cached data.
- Respect CacheService size limits (about 100 KB per value); chunk or skip caching large values.
- Never cache real-time or critical data without a freshness rule.

### 6.4 Google Classroom / Google APIs

- Never call Classroom APIs merely to render data already stored in the Dashboard Sheet/cache.
- Avoid duplicate course, roster, topic, coursework, Meet, Directory, Reports, Drive, or other API calls.
- Reuse data already loaded during the request.
- Batch/paginate only when required.
- Retry only transient errors with bounded backoff.
- Do not add a new API call if an existing Sheet/cache/helper can provide the required value.

### 6.5 Browser / `google.script.run`

- Minimize server round trips; reuse the existing request batching where it exists.
- Prevent duplicate and overlapping requests; do not trigger the same load from multiple initialization paths.
- Avoid unnecessary polling; pause nonessential polling when the tab is hidden; preserve existing realtime behavior where required.
- Lazy-load expensive tabs/data when this does not change existing behavior.
- Return only the data required by the current UI; do not send full datasets unnecessarily.
- Refresh only the affected UI section; never rebuild the entire Dashboard for one change. Preserve existing data on screen during background refresh and avoid unnecessary loading/flicker (details in §8).

### 6.6 Writes

- Batch Google Sheet writes with `setValues()` where safe; no cell-by-cell writes.
- Use `LockService` for read-modify-write operations.
- Keep writes idempotent.

---

# 7. Data Access Pattern

Checklist for each request (rules in §6.2–6.3):

1. Determine the minimum data actually required.
2. Read each required source once where practical.
3. Normalize once.
4. Build indexed maps for repeated lookups.
5. Reuse those maps for all subsequent operations.
6. Return only required fields.
7. Cache only data whose freshness rules permit caching.

Do not blindly cache real-time data.

---

# 8. Auto-Refresh and UI State

Existing APS behavior includes quiet background refresh and targeted realtime updates.

When adding refresh behavior:
- do not introduce full-page reloads;
- do not use `location.reload()` unless explicitly required;
- avoid rebuilding unrelated views;
- preserve active search/filter/input/scroll state and keep existing data on screen until new data arrives;
- prevent overlapping refreshes;
- update only changed DOM sections where practical;
- keep specialized working screens stable while users are editing/submitting data.

Dropdown/filter changes should refresh the relevant result automatically when that is the existing UX pattern.

---

# 9. Identity, Roles, and Security

Use the existing APS authorization system. Do not invent a second role system.

Server-side authorization is mandatory for every protected operation.

Never trust:
- client-provided email
- client-provided role
- localStorage
- hidden buttons
- hidden fields
- URL parameters for authorization

Use the authenticated Google identity from the existing server-side mechanism.

Typical roles include:
- Super Admin / Admin
- Headmaster / HM
- VP / BOD / other configured staff roles
- Teacher
- Student

**Important:** actual role lists, role overrides, access-control configuration, and current permissions must be read from the current code/configuration. Do not copy historical hardcoded email lists from this prompt into new code.

For every new protected tab/action:
- add/reuse the existing access-control mechanism;
- enforce authorization on the server;
- hide/disable unauthorized UI only as a UX layer, never as the security layer.

---

# 10. APSID and Student Identity

When APSID is derived from an APS email:

`name_aps1234@avvaiyarpadasalai.org → APS1234`

Extract the text after `_` and before `@`, normalize consistently, preferably uppercase.

Use `APSXXX` only when APSID genuinely cannot be determined.

Never replace a valid APSID with `APSXXX`.

For student-level records, prefer stable identifiers:
- APSID
- APS email
- Google user ID where available
- Zoho Student ID where available

Do not use display name as the primary identity key.

# 14. Caching

Use the existing CacheService/Script Properties caching architecture where appropriate.

Good candidates:

Do not create a new caching system if an existing helper already handles the same data.

The Dashboard is the integration hub for Zoho CRM.

Before completion:

- compare before/after (§6.1): Sheet reads, server calls, API calls, payload size, cache usage;
- verify no sheet/range is read more than once per request and no Sheet reads remain inside loops;
- verify lookups use indexed maps, not repeated scans;

### Regression
Compare the working tree with `CURRENT_PROD_CODE` and identify:
- unintended behavior changes
- duplicate functionality
- dead code introduced by the change
- duplicate API calls
- redundant Sheet operations
- UI regressions
- authorization regressions
- duplicate triggers

Do not remove existing production code merely because it looks unused. Remove only newly introduced dead code when dependencies are verified.

Do not claim a test passed unless it was actually executed.

If execution is unavailable, state:

**Not executed — environment/authorization required.**

12. Did I protect secrets and sensitive data?
13. Did I update the architecture documentation?
14. Did I compare the result with `CURRENT_PROD_CODE`?
15. Did I make the smallest safe change?

Key performance question:

> **Did I reduce unnecessary Google Sheet reads, duplicate server calls, API calls, DOM rendering, and repeated data processing without changing existing functionality?**

Also confirm: correctness, data accuracy, and security are unchanged, and the before/after measurement (§6.1) is reported.

# 26. Implementation Constraints

- Do not add a new API/library/framework/external service merely for convenience or performance.
- Do not rewrite working modules unnecessarily.
- Do not duplicate existing helpers.
- Do not modify `CURRENT_PROD_CODE`.
- Do not change unrelated workflows.
- Prefer configuration over hardcoded deployment-specific values.
- Prefer existing architecture over new architecture.
- Prefer small, reversible changes.
- Keep the dashboard fast without sacrificing correctness.

Priority:

**Correctness > Data Integrity > Security > Existing Functionality > Performance > UX Polish > Code Simplification**

# 27. Current APS Reference — How to Resolve Conflicts

This generic prompt intentionally does **not** contain the complete historical release log.

When a requirement appears to conflict with an older statement:

1. Current working `Code.gs` / `Dashboard.html` behavior is the implementation baseline.
2. Current `dashboard-architecture-and-config.md` is the architecture reference.
3. `CURRENT_PROD_CODE` is the immutable production comparison baseline.
4. The user's current request is the requested change.
5. The newest confirmed configuration/code wins over historical notes.
6. If the conflict affects security, data ownership, permissions, or destructive behavior, stop and ask before making the change.

Never copy historical email addresses, schedules, role lists, sheet structures, API assumptions, or feature states into new code without verifying them.

---

# 28. Required Working Sequence

Always follow this sequence:

**Read → Map dependencies → Identify reusable code → Plan smallest change → Implement → Optimize → Validate → Compare with production → Update documentation → Report**

Do not skip the production comparison or validation step.

# 31. Completion Standard

The implementation is complete only when:

# PART B — APS Dashboard on Azure: Migration Rules (Apps Script → Azure)

Part A (the generic APS Dashboard prompt above) applies IN FULL to this project.
Part B adds the rules for the Azure migration. Where Part B and Part A differ, Part B
wins only for the Azure code in this project; Apps Script production rules stay unchanged.

---

## B1. Projects and folders

Azure project (this repository):
`C:\Users\AmChaTS\PycharmProjects\APS-Dashboard-Azure`

Live Apps Script project (still production until cut-over):
`C:\Users\AmChaTS\PycharmProjects\APS-Classroom-Dashboard`

Production snapshot — READ ONLY, never modify, delete, rename or overwrite:
`C:\Users\AmChaTS\PycharmProjects\APS-Classroom-Dashboard\CURRENT_PROD_CODE`

Layout of this project:

| Folder | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `src/` | Azure app (Node.js + TypeScript, Express on Azure App Service) |
| `public/` | Browser files: `Dashboard.html` (synced copy) and `aps-gas-shim.js` |
| `test/` | Azure unit, API and parity tests |
| `tools/` | sync-gas, sync-dashboard, sync-prompt, run-gas-regression, e2e-browser |
| `infra/` | Bicep (App Service, Key Vault, App Insights, managed identity) |
| `gas-source/` | Reference copy of the live Apps Script + its regression suite |
| `docs/` | PHASE notes, deploy workflow copy, `reference/`, `prompt/` |

Rules:
- `gas-source/` is a **reference copy**. Refresh it only with `npm run sync-gas`. Do not hand-edit it.
- Apps Script changes are made in `APS-Classroom-Dashboard` (following Part A), then synced here.
- Never copy, print, zip, send or commit `ENV_VARIABLE_*.gs` or any file holding secrets.
- `aps_dashboard_Azure_prompt.txt` is generated. Edit Part A in the generic prompt and Part B in
  `docs/prompt/azure_prompt_addendum.txt`, then run `npm run sync-prompt`.

---

## B2. Migration approach (strangler pattern)

- Move one module at a time. Apps Script stays the live system until each module is proven on Azure.
- Every user-visible behavior must stay identical: same tabs, labels, roles, messages, emails,
  Sheet columns and audit records. "Do NOT change existing features" (Part A) applies to the port.
- Keep the **same function names** as `Code.gs`. The browser still calls `google.script.run.<fn>`;
  `public/aps-gas-shim.js` sends it to `POST /api/run/<fn>`, answered by `src/api/registry.ts`.
- A function not yet ported must return the standard "not on Azure yet" message — never a fake result.
- Helper functions ending in `_` are never callable from the browser.
- Google Sheets remain the system of record until a later phase explicitly approves a database move.

---

## B3. Parity is mandatory

For every ported function:
1. Read the current `Code.gs` implementation (and its `CURRENT_PROD_CODE` version) first.
2. Port the logic with the same inputs, outputs, ordering, rounding, messages and edge cases.
3. Add a parity test that runs the `Code.gs` function in gasmock (`gas-source/`) and the TypeScript
   port on the same data, and compares results.
4. Run `npm test` and `npm run test:gas`. Report results exactly as executed.

Generated or shared tables (for example the Access Control catalog) must be derived from `Code.gs`,
not retyped by hand.

---

## B4. Identity, roles and security on Azure

- Sign-in: Google OAuth code flow, single-use state nonce, ID token verified server-side.
- Allowed domains, role order, APSID rules and Access Control come from the ported Code.gs logic.
- Every protected endpoint starts with `requireSession` / `requireTab` — server-side, always.
- Never trust client role, client email, hidden buttons or browser parameters (Part A §9).
- `DEV_LOGIN` is for local development only and must be refused in Azure and production.
- Session tokens, OAuth codes, ID tokens, access tokens and service-account keys must never appear in
  logs, error messages, the browser, audit records or test output.

---

## B5. Secrets and configuration

- All secrets live in **Azure Key Vault**, read by the App Service **managed identity**
  through Key Vault references. Never in code, `.env` files committed to git, Bicep, or the workflow.
- `.env.example` lists setting names only, never values.
- Google access uses a **service account with domain-wide delegation**, scopes kept to the minimum.
- Deployment uses **GitHub Actions with OIDC** (no long-lived Azure credentials in GitHub).
- An unresolved Key Vault reference counts as "not set"; the app must start safely and explain what is missing.

---

## B6. Apps Script → Azure mapping

| Apps Script | Azure equivalent |
|---|---|
| `doGet` / HtmlService | Express `GET /` + `src/web/render.ts` (known scriptlets only) |
| `google.script.run` | `aps-gas-shim.js` → `POST /api/run/:fn` (`{ok}` / `{err}`) |
| `SpreadsheetApp` reads | Sheets API `values.batchGet` + TTL cache with in-flight de-duplication |
| `SpreadsheetApp` writes | Sheets API `batchUpdate` / `values.batchUpdate` — one batched call per action |
| `CacheService` | In-process TTL cache now; Azure Cache for Redis only if scale requires it |
| `PropertiesService` | Planned per phase (Key Vault for secrets; table/Sheet storage for data) |
| `LockService` | Planned per phase (single-instance lock now; distributed lock before scale-out) |
| Time triggers | Planned: Azure Functions timer triggers (one scheduler, same schedules) |
| `MailApp` / `GmailApp` | Gmail API via the service account, same templates and branding |
| `ClassroomApp` / Admin APIs | Google REST APIs via the service account, same course filters |
| `Logger` / execution log | Application Insights (no secrets, no tokens, no personal data beyond what is needed) |

Do not choose a new service for a mapped item without stating why and getting approval.

---

## B7. Performance on Azure (adds to Part A §6)

- Read each Sheet range at most once per request; batch ranges with `batchGet`.
- Cache by the same freshness rules Apps Script uses; never cache realtime data longer than Apps Script did.
- Keep payloads at least as small as the Apps Script version; do not send fields the browser does not use.
- Retry Google API calls only on transient errors, with bounded back-off.
- Measure before/after where practical and report it.

---

## B8. Infrastructure and deployment

- Infrastructure changes go in `infra/main.bicep` only — no manual portal-only changes without recording them.
- Node.js version must be a **supported LTS** and identical in `package.json` engines, Bicep and the workflow.
- The workflow lives at `.github/workflows/azure-deploy.yml` (copy kept at `docs/azure-deploy.yml.txt`;
  keep both identical).
- `/healthz` must expose no data or secrets.
- Do not deploy, create Azure resources, or change Google Workspace settings unless the user asks.

---

## B9. Testing and reporting on Azure

Required before reporting a change as done:
- `npm test` (TypeScript build + Azure tests, including parity tests)
- `npm run test:gas` when Apps Script reference behavior is involved
- `npm run e2e` when the page, shim or sign-in flow changes

Follow Part A's rule: never claim a test passed unless it was actually run. Anything that needs
Azure, real Google sign-in, real Sheets, or GitHub Actions and was not run must be reported as:
**"Not executed — environment/authorization required."**

The final report (Part A §25) must also state:
- which Code.gs functions were ported or changed, and their parity test results;
- any setting, secret or Azure resource the user must add;
- what still runs only on Apps Script.

---

## B10. Azure self-review (adds to Part A §24)

Before finishing, confirm:
- [ ] Behavior matches Code.gs (parity test added and run).
- [ ] Same function names; no underscore helper exposed.
- [ ] Every endpoint enforces session and tab access server-side.
- [ ] No secret, token or key in code, logs, errors, browser or tests.
- [ ] `CURRENT_PROD_CODE` and the live Apps Script project were not modified.
- [ ] `gas-source/` changed only through `npm run sync-gas`.
- [ ] Sheet reads batched and cached by the existing freshness rules.
- [ ] Bicep, workflow and engines agree on Node version and settings.
- [ ] Docs updated (`README.md`, `docs/PHASE*.md`) to match the actual implementation.
- [ ] `docs/APS_Dashboard_Azure_Guide.md` updated (what is on Azure, settings, deploy, troubleshooting, change log).
- [ ] Generated files current (`npm run gen-gas`; `npm test` fails otherwise); new sheets added to the snapshot list.
- [ ] Parity test seeds REAL rows for every new part and asserts each part actually appeared (not "empty = empty").
- [ ] Anything that writes (save buttons, emails, test sends) is switched off on Azure or reported as NOT_ON_AZURE_YET.
- [ ] Settings / secrets the user must add are listed with the exact command (PowerShell-safe quoting).

## B11. How a screen moves to Azure (Phase 2 method — use this, do not hand-port)

1. **Find the Code.gs read function** the browser calls (same name, e.g. `getClassTeacherAvailabilityView`).
2. **Copy, never retype, Code.gs logic:**
   - pure rules (no Apps Script service) → `tools/gen-gas-helpers.js` → `src/gas/classes.generated.ts`;
   - Sheet readers / whole read endpoints → add the function to a feature list in `tools/gen-gas-scope.js` and run
     `npm run gen-gas`. The tool lists every name used but neither copied nor provided; add those until it passes.
     It refuses Classroom / Gmail / Drive / triggers / locks / setProperty. It indexes top-level `function`, `var`,
     `const` and `let`.
3. **Read-only runtime** (`src/gas/runtime.ts`): sheets are a snapshot read through the Sheets API (whole sheet,
   cached 60 s, Apps Script value types incl. Date cells in the spreadsheet time zone). Writes to existing sheets or
   settings throw `READ_ONLY`; a missing sheet exists only in memory; a sheet that exists but was not read throws
   (add it to `MAIN_SHEETS` / `ATTENDANCE_SHEETS` in `src/api/endpoints/classes.ts`). Session / tab checks:
   Azure checks the token (`requireSession`), the copied code gets the same session and the same Access Control
   switches. Settings come from App Service (same names as Script Properties; never secrets) + the role lists.
4. **Register the endpoint** with the Code.gs name in `src/api/endpoints/…`; switch off anything that writes
   (e.g. `canSubmit` / `canSendTest` = false) until that write moves.
5. **Parity test** in `test/classes.parity.test.ts`: run the Code.gs function in the Apps Script mock and the Azure
   endpoint on the same seeded Sheets for every role (incl. refusals); compare the full result; assert every new part
   had real data. Add a browser check in `tools/e2e-browser.js`.
6. **Docs:** `docs/PHASE2.md`, `docs/APS_Dashboard_Azure_Guide.md`, README; list any new app setting.

Known Apps Script mock limit: new mock sheets have 26 columns — widen them in the test (`sh.maxCols`) when a
header is longer, or Code.gs fails quietly in the mock.

---

## B12. Current state (keep updated)

- Azure web app `aps-dashboard-ap` (resource group `rg-aps-dashboard`, Key Vault `kv-apsdashboardapu7zau2j`),
  Node 22 LTS, deployed by GitHub Actions (`vsugadev/APS-Dashboard-Azure`, managed identity `id-aps-github`, OIDC).
- On Azure (read-only): sign-in, sessions, roles, Access Control (view), Classes view (`getDashboardData`) incl.
  Sheet-based card parts, `getMyCountryPreference`, Teacher Availability (`getClassTeacherAvailabilityView`),
  Active Directory (`getDirectoryIndex`, role-tiered; Onboarding Status is browser-side).
- Live-data passes (presence / last login / onboarded / hidden staff) have ONE Azure implementation
  (`liveEmptyPasses`, provided to the copied code) — never write a second one.
- Live Apps Script dashboard remains production for every user; Azure is not yet announced to users.
- Phase 3 (live data in Script / User Properties) and every write still to come.
